 Order

Present petition has been filed by applicant under Section 483(2) of BNSS, 2023 for cancellation of bail granted to respondents No.1 Ismail Shah vide order dated 10/07/2023 passed in Cr. Appeal No.6531/2023.

2. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that there are three cases of identical nature i.e. under Section 376 of IPC against the present applicant, therefore, bail granted to respondent No.1 be cancelled.

It is also urged that present case pertains to offence under Section 376, 376(2)(n), of IPC and Sections 3(2)(v-a), 3(2)(v), 3(1)(2), 3(1)(w)(i) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
Crime No.69/2020 also pertains to offence under Section 376 of the IPC.
Further, Crime No.39/2024 also pertains to offence under Section 376 of the IPC.
It is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42151 2 MCRC-52931-2024 evident that the applicant has misused the bail granted to him.
On above grounds, it is urged that the bail granted to the respondent No.1 be cancelled.

3. Learned counsel for respondent No.1 submits that while granting bail to the respondent no.1,
learned trial court has taken into consideration Crime No.69/2020 and present case pertains to Crime No.243/2023.
It is also urged that so far as Crime No.39/2024 is concerned, the applicant has been acquitted by the trial Court vide its judgment dated 21.07.2025 passed in ST No.123/2024.

sentences.text: Therefore, no case for cancellation of bail is made out.
4. Learned counsel for State submits that bail granted to respondent no.1 by impugned order be cancelled.
5. Heard.
Perused the record of the case.

6. Before discussing the case on merits, it would be appropriate to reproduce para 5 of the impugned order which reads as under :
"5.
On going through facts and circumstances of the case; it is found that prosecutrix has lodged as many as five FIRs of rape against different persons.
Two FIRs have been lodged against appellant.

Prosecution version is difficult to believe that prosecutrix is again and again falling victim of false promise to marry and entering into relationship and again filing false FIR against accused persons."
7.
From aforesaid, it is evident that offence pertaining to Crime No.69/2020 was taken into consideration by this Court while granting bail to respondent No.1 vide impugned order.
Crime No.243/2023 pertains to the instant case.
So far as Crime No.39/2024 is concerned, it it evident that respondent no.1 has been acquitted by learned IIIrd ASJ, Seoni vide judgment dated 21.07.2025 passed in ST No.123/2024.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42151 3 MCRC-52931-2024 8.
Hence, in view of the aforesaid, no case for grant of cancellation of bail is made out.
9. Therefore, the petition filed by the applicant is dismissed.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE m/-
